## Intent

A primitive is unsafe in a composition that nobody has deployed. Post- mortem addition: it separates "this building block can be misused" from "this product can be attacked".

## Detection signals

Signals describe the absence of a deployed consumer: "no deployed instance", "the maker must choose to deploy this", "a design choice no deployed strategy makes".

Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the full text of the
draft finding, subject to the engine rules below.

**Fires when at least one of these matches:**

```text
  economically rational
  permitted by the guards?
  the maker (must|could|would) (choose|deploy|author)
  no (deployed|shipped|documented) (instance|strategy|consumer)
  a design choice no deployed
  no permissionless consumer
```

## Escape hatches

Three suppression patterns, each of which requires an ASSERTION that a deployment exists. They are deliberately narrow: a bare "deployed instance" would also match "no deployed instance exists", which is the opposite signal. This escape hatch once suppressed its own positive case, which is how the assertion requirement was found.

**Suppressed when any of these matches anywhere in the finding:**

```text
  a deployed (instance|strategy|consumer)[^.]{0,40}(exists|exhibits|shows|demonstrates)
  the deployed (instance|strategy|configuration)[^.]{0,40}(exhibits|shows|demonstrates)
  shipped in the
```

## Known false-positive modes

These are the shapes where the rule fires on something it should not. They are the
reason a firing is a prompt to check, not a verdict.

- A finding where the deployed consumer exists but the report describes it in words the assertion patterns do not match.
- A finding about a primitive that the *program itself* deploys through a factory, so the deployment is implicit.
- A report that names a deployed instance and is flagged on a separate sentence about a hypothetical composition.

## Synthetic examples

Both examples are synthetic. They describe no real report and no real target.

**Fires:** "The maker must choose to deploy this composition; no deployed instance exists."

**Does not fire:** "The deployed instance at the documented strategy exhibits this behaviour."

## Corrective action

Name the real deployment the attack needs, or downgrade the claim to the primitive layer. A primitive unsafe in a configuration nobody runs is not a product vulnerability.
